description: Every important scientific assumption or numerical parameter range, mapped to the source that justifies it. Verification status distinguishes sources located with enough confidence to build against from claims that still need to be tracked down before appearing on the poster.

verification_status_legend.verified: Full citation confirmed and will be printed on the poster/methodology as-is
verification_status_legend.to_verify_phase_2: Source is expected to exist and is believed correct, but full citation details (exact year/journal/DOI) must be confirmed before use
verification_status_legend.SOURCE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED: No credible source has been confirmed yet; must not be cited until verified, per project rules

sources.parameter_or_claim: CO2 solubility constant (K0) as a function of temperature and salinity
sources.source: Weiss, R. F. (1974). Carbon dioxide in water and seawater: the solubility of a non-ideal gas. Marine Chemistry.
sources.why_used: Standard, widely used formulation for CO2 gas solubility in seawater

sources.parameter_or_claim: Carbonic acid dissociation constants K1 and K2
sources.source: Lueker, T. J., Dickson, A. G., & Keeling, C. D. (2000). Ocean pCO2 calculated from dissolved inorganic carbon, alkalinity, and equations for K1 and K2.
sources.why_used: Widely adopted constants for carbonate speciation calculations, valid over typical surface-ocean T/S range

sources.parameter_or_claim: Boric acid dissociation constant (KB)
sources.source: Dickson, A. G. (1990). Thermodynamics of the dissociation of boric acid in synthetic seawater.
sources.why_used: Standard constant needed to compute total alkalinity from carbonate speciation

sources.parameter_or_claim: Water dissociation constant (KW)
sources.source: Millero, F. J. (1995). Thermodynamics of the carbon dioxide system in the oceans.
sources.why_used: Standard constant for the water dissociation term in the total alkalinity equation

sources.parameter_or_claim: Total borate concentration from salinity
sources.source: Uppstrom, L. R. (1974); Lee, K. et al. (2010)
sources.why_used: Relates total borate to salinity, needed for the borate term in total alkalinity

sources.parameter_or_claim: Aragonite and calcite solubility products (Ksp)
sources.source: Mucci, A. (1983). The solubility of calcite and aragonite in seawater at various salinities, temperatures, and one atmosphere total pressure.
sources.why_used: Required to compute aragonite and calcite saturation states (Omega)

sources.parameter_or_claim: Calcium ion concentration from salinity
sources.source: Riley, J. P., & Tongudai, M. (1967). The major cation/chlorinity ratios in seawater.
sources.why_used: Conservative relationship used to estimate [Ca2+] from salinity for saturation-state calculations

sources.parameter_or_claim: Primary carbonate system solver
sources.source: Humphreys, M. P. et al. (2022). PyCO2SYS: marine carbonate system calculations in Python.
sources.why_used: Established, peer-reviewed, community-standard software for carbonate system speciation, used as the primary calculation engine

sources.parameter_or_claim: Reference/check values for validating the carbonate system solver
sources.source: Dickson, A. G., Sabine, C. L., & Christian, J. R. (Eds.) (2007). Guide to Best Practices for Ocean CO2 Measurements.
sources.why_used: Standard reference guide containing check values used to validate solver correctness (rule V11)

sources.parameter_or_claim: Foundational carbonate chemistry theory (Revelle factor, buffering)
sources.source: Zeebe, R. E., & Wolf-Gladrow, D. (2001). CO2 in Seawater: Equilibrium, Kinetics, Isotopes.
sources.why_used: Standard reference textbook for the theoretical carbonate-system relationships used throughout the project

sources.parameter_or_claim: Total alkalinity - salinity relationship used to generate baseline alkalinity from sampled salinity
sources.source: Lee, K. et al. (2006). Global relationships of total alkalinity with salinity and temperature in surface waters of the world's oceans.
sources.why_used: Provides an empirically grounded relationship so sampled salinity and baseline alkalinity covary realistically instead of being independently randomized

sources.parameter_or_claim: Baseline surface-ocean DIC and pH ranges used for plausibility checks (rule V5)
sources.source: GLODAPv2 (Lauvset, S. K. et al.); Jiang, L.-Q. et al. (2019) surface ocean pH climatology
sources.why_used: Observed global surface-ocean data products used to bound realistic baseline chemistry ranges

sources.parameter_or_claim: Atmospheric CO2 concentration used as the reference/background level (~425 ppm)
sources.source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory (GML)
sources.why_used: Authoritative, continuously updated source for current atmospheric CO2 concentration

sources.parameter_or_claim: Overview of Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement as a carbon dioxide removal approach
sources.source: Renforth, P., & Henderson, G. (2017). Assessing ocean alkalinity for carbon sequestration. Reviews of Geophysics.
sources.why_used: Foundational review establishing the OAE concept, mechanisms, and deployment considerations

sources.parameter_or_claim: Research priorities and open questions for ocean-based carbon dioxide removal
sources.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) (2021). A Research Strategy for Ocean-Based Carbon Dioxide Removal and Sequestration.
sources.why_used: Authoritative national-academy assessment used to frame deployment-scale considerations and research needs

sources.parameter_or_claim: Equilibrated CO2 uptake efficiency (~0.75-0.85 mol CO2 per mol alkalinity) and the concept of incomplete equilibration
sources.source: He, J., & Tyka, M. D. (2023). Limits and CO2 equilibration of near-coast alkalinity enhancement.
sources.why_used: Directly supports the two-state (immediate vs. equilibrated) modeling approach and the equilibration-fraction parameter

sources.parameter_or_claim: Aragonite saturation state threshold associated with abiotic/runaway calcium carbonate precipitation (Omega approx. 5)
sources.source: Moras, C. A. et al. (2022); Hartmann, J. et al. (2023)
sources.why_used: Basis for the precipitation-risk index and threshold used in the perturbation analysis

sources.parameter_or_claim: Best-practice guidance for OAE research methodology
sources.source: Oschlies, A. et al. (2023). Guide to Best Practices in Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Research.
sources.why_used: Field-wide methodological guidance used to frame assumptions and limitations

sources.parameter_or_claim: Broader ocean acidification and carbon dioxide removal context
sources.source: IPCC AR6 (Sixth Assessment Report)
sources.why_used: Authoritative synthesis used for background framing on ocean acidification and CDR approaches

sources.parameter_or_claim: Regulatory pH-change guideline (e.g., +/- 0.2 pH units at discharge/mixing zones) proposed as a possible perturbation-threshold reference
sources.source: Not yet located
sources.why_used: Would provide a regulatory (rather than purely experimental) anchor for the perturbation-risk threshold

sources.parameter_or_claim: Exact mesocosm/experimental total alkalinity addition ranges used to justify the 150-500 umol/kg 'stress test' dose levels
sources.source: Not yet located
sources.why_used: Would confirm that the upper dose ladder matches ranges actually used in published OAE mesocosm experiments
